abstract.t:
Ethernet VPN (EVPN) Integrated Routing and Bridging (IRB) distributes Layer 2 and Layer 3 reachability through BGP. In a large stretched broadcast domain, traditional IRB can cause every Provider Edge (PE) to install MAC and IP addresses for every endpoint in the subnet thus resulting in exhaustion of forwarding resources (MAC-VRF and IP-VRF) on the PEs - i.e., route population is approximately proportional to the number of endpoints in every stretched subnet imported by the PE
[Optimized-IRB] proposes a solution to alleviate the MAC-VRF resource consumption by terminating ARP/ND messages on the PE and providing L3 forwarding (routing) for both intra and inter subnets. Therefore, eliminating the need for MAC lookups and the maintenance of MAC addresses in MAC-VRF for IP hosts. However, this solution does not solve the IP-VRF resource consumption issue as IP host addresses still need to be maintained in IP-VRF for both the locally connected hosts and the remote hosts.
This problem is particularly pronounced in campus networks where most subnets are stretched across the entire campus (and thus all access switches) and the access switches used as EVPN-IRB PE devices have significantly smaller forwarding tables and hence limit the total endpoint scale that can be attached to stretched subnets across the network. This document defines an EVPN Subnet Slicing solution to horizontally scale stretched subnets across the network without being constrained by any PE's forwarding table size. The solution enables access layer PE devices to maintain only locally attached host routes and allows host routes to be distributed across distribution or aggregation layer PE devices as opposed to each PE maintaining all host IP routes.
